Brian GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE had left London and was believed to have gone abroad. Enquiries, however, had failed to reveal his destination. KRIVITSKY himself stated that in the Spring of 1936 through his intervention, Brian GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE had achieved his ambition of going to the U.S.S.R. to take up residence there.

The little we know of Brian GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE's activities after he had left the U.K. is supplied by KRIVITSKY and Mrs. GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE, Brian's mother.

According to KRIVITSKY, Brian GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE became a pupil at ABRAMOFF's radio school in Moscow. In 1937 he was sent to Spain as a radio operator. KRIVITSKY described him as an ardent Communist and idealist who fell foul of the O.G.P.U. on account of his criticism of Soviet methods in Spain. As a result the O.G.P.U. had lured him on to a Soviet ship by means of a trick, and had transported him to Odessa as a prisoner. On 12th April he had been thrust into an O.G.P.U. dungeon in Moscow. Brian GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE, while in Spain, had been known by the nickname "FRIEND". KRIVITSKY published an account of the kidnapping of "FRIEND" in his book "I was Stalin's Agent". (pp. 123 - 124).

In 1939 Mrs. GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE corresponded with KRIVITSKY, in the hope that he might assist her in tracing her son. She had last heard from Brian in April 1937; until then he had written to her regularly from Valencia, where he was employed as a radio transmitter in the Russian Embassy. According to her information he had offended the Russian Ambassador who had found some pretext for sending him to Barcelona whence he had disappeared. When he first went to Spain, a passport bearing a Spanish name had been given him in Paris, to enable him to cross the frontier.

In 1939 the Foreign Office asked the British Embassy in Moscow to make enquiries about Brian GOOLD-VERSCHOYLE. The Embassy replied that such enquiries would not only prove fruitless but would embarrass the treaty negotiations which were then taking place between the U.S.S.R. and the U.K.
